# Sales Navigator search recipes

LinkedIn changes its interface and plan entitlements. Use the filter labels currently shown in the user's Sales Navigator account and check the live UI before telling the user a filter is available.

The official filter documentation describes lead filters such as current company, current job title, function, seniority, geography, industry, company headcount, changed jobs in the last 90 days, posted on LinkedIn in the last 30 days, profile views, buyer intent, connections and shared experiences. Account filters include headquarters, industry, headcount, revenue, department headcount growth, job opportunities, recent activity and buyer intent. Some filters are plan-dependent.

## Search 1 — Founder-led web and full-stack projects

Lead filters:
- Geography: United States;
- Current title: Founder, Co-founder, Owner, CEO, President;
- Seniority: Owner, CXO, Partner, where available;
- Industry: choose only relevant verticals;
- Company headcount: start with a small/midsize range and refine after seeing results;
- Recent updates: posted in the last 30 days or changed jobs in the last 90 days, when relevant.

Account filters:
- Headquarters: United States;
- Company headcount and annual revenue: use as rough sizing, not proof of budget;
- Recent activity or job opportunities: add only when it improves the service fit.

## Search 2 — Engineering and product buyers

Lead filters:
- Geography: United States;
- Current title: CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Engineering, Engineering Director, Head of Product, VP Product;
- Function: Engineering or Product;
- Seniority: Director, VP, CXO;
- Company headcount: use a range consistent with the intended project size;
- Recent updates: posted on LinkedIn or changed jobs, if useful.

Prioritize companies with a current engineering or product trigger, not every company with a CTO.

## Search 3 — QA and testing opportunities

Lead filters:
- Current title: CTO, VP Engineering, Head of QA, QA Director, QA Lead, Engineering Manager, Test Automation Lead;
- Function: Engineering / Quality, where available;
- Seniority: Manager, Director, VP, CXO;
- Geography: United States;
- Recent updates: job change or recent post.

Account research:
- current QA/SDET/test automation job openings;
- active product release cadence;
- integrations or complex customer workflows;
- evidence of release-quality or regression pressure.

A QA job opening is not proof of outsourcing demand. Use it to prioritize research and identify the relevant buyer.

## Search 4 — Shopify and e-commerce

Lead filters:
- Current title: Founder, Owner, Head of E-commerce, E-commerce Director, Digital Director, Head of Growth;
- Industry: retail, consumer goods, apparel, beauty or the specific store vertical;
- Geography: United States;
- Seniority: Owner, Director, VP, CXO.

Account research:
- verify the store platform before labeling it Shopify;
- inspect product discovery, mobile UX and the public purchase path;
- look for launches, new product lines, migrations or hiring.

## Search 5 — AI automation and operations

Lead filters:
- Current title: COO, Head of Operations, Operations Director, RevOps Lead, CTO, Head of Systems;
- Function: Operations, Information Technology, Engineering or Business Development;
- Seniority: Manager, Director, VP, CXO;
- Geography: United States.

Account research:
- identify manual handoffs or repetitive workflows from public evidence;
- look for hiring that signals systems, integration or automation needs;
- describe the operational opportunity without claiming hidden inefficiency.

## Search 6 — Recover Revenue home-service operators

Use only for the Recover Revenue lane.

Lead filters:
- Current title: Owner, Founder, President, General Manager, Marketing Director, Operations Director;
- Industry: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, remodeling and adjacent service categories;
- Geography: United States, narrowed to the states or metros the user specifies;
- Company headcount: use a broad small-business range, then verify manually.

Account research:
- official company website;
- services and service areas;
- inquiry/contact path;
- mobile experience;
- public reviews and business updates;
- evidence of expansion or new service lines.

Do not scrape Google Maps or LinkedIn at scale. Use public search and manual review.

## Saved-search handoff

When the user asks for saved searches, produce a table with:
- search name;
- lead or account search;
- exact filters;
- include/exclude values;
- why it exists;
- what to do when the result count is too large or too small.

Do not claim a search was saved or an alert enabled unless the user actually completes that action in Sales Navigator or an authorized tool confirms it.
